Chapter 8 (al-bāb al-thāmin): On the four seasonal quarters (thawāqīf) and the revolving seasons that pertain specially to them

The master — may God, exalted is He, have mercy upon him — said: Know — may God, exalted is He, grant success to me and to you in obedience to Him — that this chapter is the pivot of this book, and that in it are recondite secrets. So when you wish to operate with these names and with the blessed and majestic seasonal quarters (thawāqīf), and with the names of the angels who govern time, and the names of the winds and the planets — know then that the year is twelve months, divided into four divisions, each division of them being three months; and the seasons are four: among them the season of summer, among them the season of autumn, among them the season of winter, and among them the season of spring. And each season of these four seasons is called a thāqūfa. The first thāqūfa is that of the season of spring, and its beginning is the twenty-fourth of Māris (March) to the twenty-fourth of Yūniya (June). The second thāqūfa is that of the season of summer, and it is the twenty-fourth day of [June] to the twenty-fourth day of Ishtanbīr (September). The third thāqūfa is that of the season of autumn, and it is from the twenty-fourth day of September to the twenty-fourth day of Dujanbīr (December). The fourth thāqūfa is that of the season of winter, and it is from the twenty-fourth day of December to the twenty-fourth day of March.

The names of the kings who govern time — it is said, the times: /fol. 45v./ the lord of the east, his name is Danyāʾil; and the lord of the west, his name is Dardiyāʾīl; and the lord of the qibla, his name is Anyāʾīl; and the lord of the south, his name is Ṣarfiyāʾīl. And the lord of the qibla is for the season of spring; and the lord of the east for the season of summer; and the lord of the south for the season of autumn; and the lord of the west for the season of winter.

The distribution of the helpers over the four cardinal directions. The helpers of the lord of the east are Darḥamiyāʾīl, Ḥarqiyāʾīl, and Samʿiyāʾīl. And the helpers of the lord of the west are Ḥabrīqīl, Qaṣmāʾīl, and Shūʿiyāʾīl. And the helpers of the lord of the qibla are Farghūʾil, Ṭākhīl, and Allūl. And the helpers of the lord of the south are Qamiyāʾīl, Marḥiyāʾīl, and Ḥarmakiyāʾīl.
Faṣl

And now there have been gathered together for you the four invocations, with their names, their angels, and their helpers, and the name of the sun and the moon and the four winds, and the name of the heaven and the earth, and everything you have need of. So lick the honey, and do not ask the honeycomb about its bees, for it has come to you white and pure. So if you are in the season of spring and have a need, then call upon the lord of the qibla. You say: In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. I adjure you, O Anyāʾil, and your helpers Farghūʾil, Ṭākhīl, and Allūl; and the winds ʿAqdadūn, Māshūl, Māsūrā, Samʿā, and Ṭabʿatayn; and the sun and the moon: Yāḥaft, Saʿsamyāh, Yūnār, Miyārij, Jarjalfah, Baṣād and her sisters, and Basīlīṣ. In the name of God, and by His name, the name with which beginning is made, Lord of the hereafter and of this present world, who has no goal and no end. [His is] what is in the heavens and what is in the earth and what is between them and what is beneath the soil. God is mighty, everlasting in bounties, most merciful of the merciful, powerful and not subject to power, subduing and not subdued, and just on the Day of Resurrection. There is no god but He, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. He is God, other than whom there is no god: the King, the All-Holy, the Peace, the Granter of Security, the Overseer, the Mighty, the Compeller, the Supremely Great. Glory be to God above what they associate with Him. He is God, the Creator, the Maker, the Fashioner. His are the Most Beautiful Names. All that is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him, and He is the Mighty, the Wise (Q 59:23–24). I ask You, O God, O al-ʿAzīz (the Mighty), that You grant me in this station of mine a mercy from Yourself, and that You fulfil my need in such-and-such a matter. Truly You are powerful over everything. And there is no power and no strength save in God, the High, the Mighty. I ask You, O God, O Lord, by Your perfect Name — O al-Ḥayy (the Living), O al-Qayyūm (the Self-Subsisting). I bear witness that everything apart from You is vain. O God, I have believed in You; there is no god but You. O Lord, there is no lord besides You. I ask You by Your mighty Name, which You have preferred above all Your names entire, that You make subservient to me the lord of this season, and the lord of the hour, and of the thāqūfa, and of the four regions, so that they may be a help to me in the fulfilling of my need, by Your leave, O God. O my God, You decree with truth, and no decree is passed against You. I adjure you, O company of spiritual kings, that you fulfil my need — by the right of Him to whom belong might and omnipotence, and by the right of the Living, the Self-Subsisting, the Everlasting who does not die, who — there is nothing like Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing; who has a name that is not forgotten, and a light that is not extinguished, and a Throne that does not pass away, and a Footstool that does not move; who sent down the Book /fol. 46r./ upon His prophet Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace. I ask You, O God, O God, O God: You are He beside whom there is no god, the Master of this world and of the hereafter. I ask You to fulfil my need, and to make subservient to me the spiritual being that serves these names. Truly You are powerful over everything.

And if you are in the time of summer, then call upon the lord of the eastern thāqūfa. You say: In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. I adjure you, O Danyāʾīl, and your helpers Darḥamiyāʾīl, Ḥarqiyāʾīl, and Samʿiyāʾil; and the winds Kaydaḥ, Masahīmūn, Masahmiyūn, Marmūd, and ʿĀdūd; and the sun and the moon: Abājūn, Nājūn, ʿAjramīsh, Barjalās, Sīlsūf, Bahwān, Balḥān, and Nīnādrūḥ. In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate, and by God; and there is no power and no strength save in God, the High, the Mighty. O God, I ask You, O Lord, in that You are living and do not die; overcoming, and are not overcome; creating, and are not created; seeing, and do not doubt; hearing, and are not uncertain; all-subduing, and are not subdued; everlasting, and are not exhausted; near, and are not far; witnessing, and are not absent; a god, and are not harmed; subduing, and do not do wrong; an eternal refuge, and are not fed; self-subsisting, and do not sleep; veiled, and are not seen; compelling, and are not oppressed; mighty, and are not to be assailed; knowing, and are not taught; strong, and do not grow weak; faithful, and do not fail; just, and do not act unfairly; rich, and do not become poor; a treasure that is not exhausted; forbearing, and do not act unjustly; inaccessible, and are not subdued; known, and are not denied; a trustee, and are not held in contempt; odd, and are not made even; single, and are not doubled; bestowing, and do not refuse; swift, and are not distracted; bountiful, and do not begrudge; mighty, and are not abased; knowing, and are not ignorant; preserving, and are not heedless; everlasting, and do not perish; known, and are not denied; answering, and do not weary; abiding, and do not wear away; one, and are not likened to any; omnipotent, and are not contended with. Thus it stands in this recension; but in others there is a second recension, which says: O God, I ask You, O Lord: O Living who does not die; creating, and are not created; self-subsisting, and do not sleep; truthful, and do not fail; just, and do not do wrong; veiled, and are not seen; inaccessible, and are not subdued; known, and are not denied; a trustee, and do not weary; swift, and are not distracted; bountiful, and do not begrudge; mighty, and are not abased; preserving, and are not heedless; everlasting, and do not perish; one, whom nothing resembles. There is no god but You, O Lord of the worlds. I ask You by Your might that You fulfil my need, and that You make subservient to me all the spiritual beings, by the right of Your majesty and the light of Your noble face. Truly that is easy for You. I adjure you, O company of spiritual beings, by God the Mighty and by His treasured, concealed Name, that you be a help to me in the fulfilling of my need, by the right of the Lord of the lofty edifice — that you assuredly answer in that to which I summon you. So hear and obey what I have commanded you, by the right of that by which I have adjured you among the mighty names of God. Come now! Haste! Speed! This very hour! May God bless you and pour blessing upon you.

And if you wish to call upon the lord of autumn, then call upon the lord of the south. You say: In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. I adjure you, O Ṣarfiyāʾil, and your helpers Qamiyāʾil, Marḥiyāʾīl, and Ḥarmakiyāʾīl; and the four winds Qandīd, Yafʿūn, Maysūr, and Kāfūn; and the sun and the moon: Sabās, Taʿābil, Huwayfīm, Mahūlāḥ, al-Nūḥ, Mithāl, Sabā, and Badūraḥ. I ask you to descend into my presence, and to comply with all /fol. 46v./ that I have commanded you and with all that I request of you. I ask You, O God, O Light of light, O Disposer of affairs, O Knower of secrets. You are God, the King, the All-Subduing; there is no god but You, and no object of worship besides You. O God, O God, by the right of these mighty names: God, God, the High, the Mighty; God, God, the Forbearing, the Generous; God, God, the Living, the Self-Subsisting; God, God, the Single, the Eternal Refuge; God, God, who did not beget and was not begotten, and to whom none is equal. I ask You by Your might, and by Your establishing Yourself upon Your Throne, that You fulfil my need, and that You make subservient to me the lord of this day, and of the hour, and of the thāqūfa, and of the four regions. Truly You are powerful over everything, for You decree with truth and no decree is passed against You; and that they be a help to me in such-and-such. O God, O

God, You are God: there is no god but You. I have believed in You and have put my trust in You. You are God: of You stands in fear all Your creation, and to You it submits itself in humility. You are the light of the heavens. You are He who has veiled Himself, so that You are not seen and Your light is not comprehended. O God, O God, O God, You are God, the Subduer. Lofty is Your majesty! You are exalted above Your Throne, and none of Your creation can describe Your greatness. O Light of light, the people of Your heavens and the people of Your earth have been illumined by Your light. O God, O God, You are too exalted to have any associate, and too magnificent to have any opposite. O Light of light, every light is quenched before Your light. O King, and every king passes away, while You are the Abiding, the Everlasting, who neither changes nor ceases. O God, O God, O God, You are the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. Have mercy upon me with a mercy whereby You extinguish from me Your wrath and Your displeasure, and whereby You grant me felicity from Yourself, and whereby You admit me into Your Garden, in which You have settled the choicest of Your creation. O God, O Most Merciful of the merciful — for I ask You that You fulfil my need, and that You make subservient to me the spiritual beings, that they may be my help in such-and-such. O God, O God, O God, O Lord of the worlds! Hasten, O Shamhūrish!

And if you are in the time of winter, then call upon the lord of the west. You say: In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. I adjure you, O Dardiyāʾīl, and your helpers Jabrīqīl, Qaṣmāʾil, and
Sūghiyāʾīl; and the winds from the earth Mujarrad, Darʿādūm, Maʿmūr, and Jarīdūm; and upon

— the sun and the moon: Jād and Jayādīm and Jālītad and Sayyīn and Lātūn and Nīshāriḥand Mudhhabāyin and Samīdrīs. I ask you to fulfil my need, by the right of that by which I speak over you. O God, I ask You by Your might, O Light of lights, O Knower of secrets! You are the King, the Compeller, the Mighty, the All-Subduing. To You belong praise, laudation, glory, and bounties. I have believed in You; there is no god but You. I ask You: O God, O Lord, O al-Raḥmān (the All-Merciful), O al-Raḥīm (the Compassionate), O al-Malik (the King), O al-Muḥīṭ (the All-Encompassing), O al-ʿAlīm (the All-Knowing), O al-Qadīr (the All-Powerful), O al-Ḥakīm (the Wise), O al-Tawwāb (the Ever-Relenting), O al-Baṣīr (the All-Seeing), O al-Wāsiʿ (the All-Embracing), O al-Badīʿ (the Wondrous Originator), O al-Samīʿ (the All-Hearing), O al-Kāfī (the Sufficient), O al-Raʾūf (the Ever-Gentle), O al-Shākir (the Thankful), O Ilāh (God), O al-Wāḥid (the One), O al-Ghafūr (the Forgiving), O al-Ḥalīm (the Forbearing), O al-Qābiḍ (the Constrictor), O al-Bāsiṭ (the Expander), O al-Ḥayy (the Living), O al-Qayyūm (the Self-Subsisting), O al-ʿAlī (the Exalted), O al-ʿAẓīm (the Magnificent), O al-Walī (the Protecting Friend), O al-Ghanī (the Self-Sufficient), O al-Ḥamīd (the Praiseworthy), O al-Wahhāb (the Bestower), O al-Qāʾim (the Upholder), O al-Sarīʿ (the Swift), O al-Raqīb (the Watcher), /fol. 47r./ O al-Ḥasīb (the Bringer to Account), O al-Shahīd (the Witness), O al-ʿAfuww (the Pardoner), O al-Mughīth (the Succourer), O al-Wakīl (the Trustee), O al-Fāṭir (the Originator), O al-Qāhir (the Subduer), O al-Laṭīf (the Subtle), O al-Qādir (the Powerful), O al-Khabīr (the All-Aware), O al-Muḥyī (the Giver of Life), O al-Mumīt (the Bringer of Death), O excellent Patron and excellent Helper, O al-Ḥafīẓ (the Preserver), O al-Qarīb (the Near), O al-Mujīb (the Answerer), O al-Qawī (the Strong), O al-Majīd (the All-Glorious), O al-Wadūd (the Loving), O Faʿʿāl li-mā yurīd (Doer of whatsoever He wills), O al-Kabīr (the Great), O al-Mutaʿāl (the Most Exalted), O al-Mannān (the Bounteous), O al-Khallāq (the Creator of all), O al-Ṣādiq (the Truthful), O al-Wārith (the Inheritor), O al-Bāʿith (the Raiser of the dead), O al-Karīm (the Generous), O al-Ḥaqq (the Truth),

O al-Mubīn (the Evident), O al-Nūr (the Light), O al-Hādī (the Guide), O al-Fattāḥ (the Opener), O al-Shakūr (the Most Thankful), O al-Ghāfir (the Forgiver), O al-Qābil (the Accepter), O Dhū al-baṭsh al-shadīd (Possessor of the mighty assault), O Dhū al-Ṭawl (Possessor of Bounty), O al-Razzāq (the Provider), O Dhū al-quwwa al-matīn (Possessor of strength, the Firm), O al-Barr (the Benign), O al-Malīk (the Sovereign), O al-Muqtadir (the Omnipotent), O al-Bāqī (the Abiding), O Dhū al-Jalāl wa-l-Ikrām (Possessor of Majesty and Honour), O al-Awwal (the First), O al-Ākhir (the Last), O al-Ẓāhir (the Manifest), O al-Bāṭin (the Hidden), O al-Quddūs (the All-Holy), O al-Salām (the Peace), O al-Muʾmin (the Granter of Security), O al-Muhaymin (the Overseer), O al-ʿAzīz (the Mighty), O al-Jabbār (the Compeller), O al-Mutakabbir (the Supremely Great), O al-Khāliq (the Creator), O al-Bāriʾ (the Maker), O al-Muṣawwir (the Shaper), O al-Mubdiʾ (the Initiator), O al-Muʿīd (the Restorer), O al-Aḥad (the

Unique), O al-Ṣamad (the Eternal Refuge), O You who have not begotten and have not been begotten, and to whom none is equal, O God, O God, O God! There is no god but You. I ask You, O Lord, by the right that these names have with You and by the might they possess in Your sight, that You make subservient to me the spiritual being of the lord of the day, and of this hour, and of this seasonal quarter (thāqūfa), and of the four regions — truly You are powerful over all things. I adjure you, O spiritual beings, that you be a help to me in the fulfilling of my need. Answer, O Khaylahūn, and rend the veil that is between me and you, by Him who said to the heavens and the earth: Come, both of you, obediently or under compulsion! They said: We have come obedient (Q 41:11).
The four seasonal quarters (thawāqīf) are now complete, together with their names; and in God lies success. And they have a signet proper to them.
Fig. 21

As for His name al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm, these are two majestic, mighty names, and the remembrance (dhikr) by means of them is mighty and noble. It profits those in dire straits and is a security for those who fear. Whoever engraves them on a Friday, in the last hour of the day, upon a signet-ring, and seals with it, will never see anything he finds hateful. And whoever multiplies the remembrance of them is treated with gentle kindness in all matters. al-Raḥmān is derived from raḥma (mercy), and al-Raḥīm likewise. And it is related that God, exalted is He, says concerning the womb (al-raḥim): ((I am al-Raḥmān, and it is the womb (al-raḥim); whoever joins it, I join him, and whoever severs it, I sever him.)) And if you look and ascertain, you will find al-Raḥmān and al-Raḥīm gathered together in Alif-Lām-Mīm and Alif-Lām-Rāʾ and the seven Ḥawāmīm. And God knows best.

And His name, exalted is He, al-Raḥmān: whoever writes it eight times in a clean vessel, with the Moon in its exaltation, and washes it off with rainwater, and one who has hardness in his heart drinks of it — that [hardness] departs from him, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And it has a square of four by four: if it is written in water and the one afflicted with burning fever is given to drink of it, it departs from him, by the leave of God, glorified and exalted. And this is its form, as you see.
Fig. 22

His name, exalted is He, al-Raḥīm: whoever sets it down, with the Moon in its exaltation, is secure from the calamities of time; and whoever sets it in a signet-ring of silver and seals with it is safe from all calamities and afflictions, and from the evil of all hateful things. And this is its form.

His name, exalted is He, al-Malik (the King): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it — the tyrants (al-farāʿina) become compliant to him, for his protection and for the fulfilling of his need. His name, exalted is He, al-Salām (the Peace): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, keeps him safe from all calamities; and whoever multiplies the remembrance of it until a [spiritual] state from it overcomes him, and then takes hold of a snake or a scorpion, it does not harm him. And it has a square of four by four: if the king carries it with him in war, he is kept safe from the assaults of calamities. And this is the form of its square, as you see.
Fig. 24

His name, exalted is He, al-Muʾmin (the Granter of Security): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it 132 times, God, exalted is He, grants him security from the evil of the plague. His name, exalted is He, al-Muhaymin (the Overseer): whoever engraves it upon a signet-ring five times, with the Moon in its exaltation, and seals with it, is protected from /fol. 48r./ the evil of the satans of humankind and of the jinn. His name, exalted is He, al-ʿAzīz (the Mighty): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it has therein a munition against the enemies of God. His name, exalted is He, al-Jabbār (the Compeller): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it becomes awe-inspiring in the sight of all people. His name, exalted is He, al-Mutakabbir (the Supremely Great): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it — his word takes effect among the secondary causes. His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Khāliq (the Creator): whoever engraves it upon a signet-ring of silver, with the ascendant one of the signs of the fiery triplicity (al-muthallathāt al-nāriyya), and seals with it, and then has intercourse with his wife — she conceives by him, by the leave of God, exalted is He. His name, exalted is He, al-Bāriʾ (the Maker): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, gives him to look upon wondrous secrets and subtle traces. His name, exalted is He, al-Muṣawwir (the Shaper): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it — the spiritual forms descend upon him within the corporeal forms. His name, exalted is He, al-Ghaffār (the All-Forgiving): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it is preserved in wars from the onslaughts of [hostile] eyes. His name, exalted is He, al-Qahhār (the All-Subduing): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it subdues his carnal appetites. His name, exalted is He, al-Wahhāb (the Bestower): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it asks God, exalted is He, for nothing but that He gives it to him. His name, exalted is He, al-Razzāq (the Provider): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, makes the means easy for him and provides for him whence he does not reckon. His name, exalted is He, al-Fattāḥ (the Opener): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God opens for him the avenues of good things, outwardly and inwardly. His name, exalted is He, al-ʿAlīm (the All-Knowing): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, causes him to speak with wisdom. His name, exalted is He, al-Qābiḍ (the Constrictor): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, bestows upon him awe-inspiring presence among all the worlds. His name, exalted is He, al-Bāsiṭ (the Expander): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it — his inmost secret is expanded. His name, exalted is He, al-Khāfiḍ (the Abaser): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it and calls down [imprecation] upon a wrongdoer is answered, if he remembers it under the [requisite] conditions. His name, exalted is He, al-Rāfiʿ (the Raiser): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, raises his standing and elevates his degree. His name, exalted is He, al-Muʿizz (the Giver of might): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, gives him might in this world and in the hereafter. His name, exalted is He, al-Mudhill (the Giver of abasement): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, abases the tyrants before him. His name, exalted is He, al-Samīʿ (the All-Hearing): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it has his supplication answered. His name, exalted is He, al-Baṣīr (the All-Seeing): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it and writes it a hundred times upon a signet-ring of glass, washes it off with rainwater, and drinks it at the breaking of the fast — his mind grows keen and his understanding strong. His name, exalted is He, al-Ḥakam (the Judge): it is fit for [obtaining] the effectiveness of one's word before rulers. His name, exalted is He, al-ʿAdl (the Just): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, inspires him in all his states. His name, exalted is He, al-Laṭīf (the Subtle): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it while an illness presses hard upon him, God, exalted is He, makes deliverance from that easy for him. His name, exalted is He, al-Khabīr (the All-Aware): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, engraves it upon a gemstone in the first hour of Friday, and places it upon his mouth — the distress of thirst does not reach him; and if he puts it into a water-jug and drinks from it, God, exalted is He, hastens for him the quenching of thirst, and he does not seek water after that. His name, exalted is He, al-Ḥalīm (the Forbearing): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it /fol. 48v./ is safe from agitation when hardships descend. His name, exalted is He, al-ʿAẓīm (the Magnificent): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it becomes great in the eyes of people. His name, exalted is He, al-Ghafūr (the Forgiving): God, exalted is He, guards him from the evil of what he fears and is wary of. His name, exalted is He, al-Shakūr (the Most Thankful): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, elevates his standing. His name, exalted is He, al-Ḥafīẓ (the Preserver): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it is preserved from the evil of the evildoers in all his movements and his stillnesses. His name, exalted is He, al-Mumīt (the Bringer of Death): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it feels no pang of hunger. His name, exalted is He, al-Ḥasīb (the Bringer to Account): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it has his need fulfilled. His name, exalted is He, al-Jalīl (the Majestic): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it finds increase in all his states and his sayings. His name, exalted is He, al-Karīm (the Generous): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it becomes one whose invocation is answered. His name, exalted is He, al-Mujīb (the Answerer): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it falls into no hardship but that he finds a way out of it. His name, exalted is He, al-Wāsiʿ (the All-Embracing): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, causes the springs of wisdom to burst forth from his heart upon his tongue. His name, exalted is He, al-Ḥakīm (the Wise): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it becomes beloved among people, in the sight of everyone. His name, exalted is He, al-Wadūd (the Loving): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, being a king — God, exalted is He, enlarges his kingdom. His name, exalted is He, al-Majīd (the All-Glorious): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it is impelled toward every good. His name, exalted is He, al-Bāʿith (the Raiser of the dead): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, makes him witness watchful vigilance (murāqaba) in his spiritual retreat (khalwa) and in all his affairs. His name, exalted is He, al-Shahīd (the Witness): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God makes his word subduing and prevailing. His name, exalted is He, al-Ḥaqq (the Truth): it has a square of five by five. Whoever engraves it upon a stone of marble, with the ascendant Scorpio (al-ʿAqrab), and places it in a house — there remains in it no snake and no scorpion but that it goes out from it, and likewise the noxious creatures, by the leave of God, exalted is He.

His name, exalted is He, al-Qawī (the Strong): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it — his spirit is strengthened and his love endures. His name, exalted is He, al-Matīn (the Firm): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it is safe from weakness of strength. His name, exalted is He, al-Walī (the Protecting Friend): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it — God takes charge of him and gives him charge. His name, exalted is He, al-Ḥamīd (the Praiseworthy): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it and writes it upon a signet-ring according to its number

— and washes it off with water and gives it to drink to one who has an illness, God, exalted is He, restores him to health from it. His name, exalted is He, al-Muḥṣī (the Reckoner): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it is secured from evil deeds. His name, exalted is He, al-Mubdiʾ (the Initiator): it is suitable for whoever wishes to make a beginning in some affair among affairs. His name, exalted is He, al-Muʿīd (the Restorer): when it is set in a square with the ascendant one of the movable signs (al-burūj al-munqaliba), and it is hung up in the path of the wind, and the person keeps on reciting the Name the whole night long over a runaway slave or a traveller, he returns to the place from which he went out, by the leave of God, exalted is He. His name, exalted is He, al-Muḥyī (the Giver of Life): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, gives life to his heart with the light of gnosis. His name, exalted is He, al-Mumīt (the Bringer of Death): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, puts to death whatever stirs in him of his dark desires. His name, exalted is He, al-Ḥayy (the Living): whoever writes it 120 times upon the door of a house, with Venus in her exaltation — then the one dwelling in it is preserved from melancholic afflictions and from evil /fol. 49r./ afflictions, by the leave of God, exalted is He. His name, exalted is He, al-Qayyūm (the Self-Subsisting): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it finds within his inmost being ample sciences and gnoses of the divine oneness. His name, exalted is He, al-Wājid (the

Finder): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God brings into being in his heart faith and pious reverence. His name, exalted is He, al-Mājid (the Glorious): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, raises his standing high, and he flees from the world. His name, exalted is He, al-Wāḥid (the One): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it grows estranged from multiplicity. His name, exalted is He, al-Aḥad (the Unique): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it becomes singular in the sciences. His name, exalted is He, al-Fard (the Sole): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, no other enters in upon him, and he feels no pang of hunger at all. His name, exalted is He, al-Ṣamad (the Eternal Refuge): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, bestows upon him a spiritual power and a gnostic strength. His name, exalted is He, al-Muqtadir (the Omnipotent): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, makes easy for him all circumstances. His name, exalted is He, al-Muqaddim (the Advancer): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God bestows upon him free disposal (taṣarruf) in the world of secondary causes. His name, exalted is He, al-Muʾakhkhir (the Deferrer): a secret whose door is locked and whose veil-covering is let down. His name, exalted is He, al-Awwal (the First): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it becomes one who presses onward toward good things. His name, exalted is He, al-Ākhir (the Last): a well-guarded secret, and its knowledge is concealed. His name, exalted is He, al-Ẓāhir (the Manifest): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God makes him privy to what is right and to the hidden aspects of affairs. His name, exalted is He, al-Bāṭin (the Hidden): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it — he does not come to anyone but that he answers him and fulfils his need. His name, exalted is He, al-Wālī (the Governor): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it becomes awe-inspiring in the sight of everyone. His name, exalted is He, al-Mutaʿāl (the Most Exalted): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, bestows upon him a luminous might and an awe befitting the Eternal Refuge (ṣamadāniyya). His name, exalted is He, al-Barr (the Benign): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it is treated with gentle kindness in all his states. His name, exalted is He, al-Tawwāb (the Ever-Relenting): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it is treated with gentle kindness. And it has a square of four by four: whoever draws it upon his palm and calls upon God by it — He turns to him in relenting. His name, exalted is He, al-Muntaqim (the Avenger): whoever writes it in a vessel, washes it off with rainwater, and gives it to drink to one who has a love for the drinking of wine — he comes to loathe it. His name, exalted is He, al-ʿAfū (the Pardoner): whoever fears a punishment from a king or from another, and remembers it according to its number, is secured from what he fears. His name, exalted is He, al-Raʾūf (the Ever-Gentle): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God is ever-gentle with him, and no tyrant's gaze falls upon him but that [God] turns his heart toward him. His name, exalted is He, Mālik al-Mulk (Master of all Dominion): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it while he is seeking a kingdom, God, exalted is He, grants it to him. His name, exalted is He, Dhū l-Jalāl wa-l-Ikrām (Possessor of Majesty and Honour): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it asks God, exalted is

He, for nothing but He gives it to him. His name, exalted is He, al-Muqsiṭ (the Equitable): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it is characterized by [spiritual] poverty (faqr) and justice in all his states. His name, exalted is He, al-Jāmiʿ (the Gatherer): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it when a slave of his has run away or a stray of his has gone missing, God restores to him that stray, by the leave of God, exalted is He. His name, exalted is He, al-Mughnī (the Enricher): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, the means of wealth and the means of this world grow abundant for him, and its provisions become ample for him; and whoever writes it and hangs it upon himself, his trade turns a profit. His name, exalted is He, al-Ghanī (the Self-Sufficient): whoever multiplies > /fol. 49v./ His name, exalted is He, al-Māniʿ (the Withholder): whoever multiplies < the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, makes him independent of created beings. His name, exalted is He, al-Māniʿ (the Withholder): whoever writes it upon the wall of a city, running all around it, in 161 places, while the preacher is upon the pulpit on Friday — God, exalted is He, guards it from the assaults of the wicked. Some of the sages set it upon a wall on the citadel of Mārdīn, and no enemy was able to take it, by the leave of God, exalted is He. His name, exalted is He, al-Ḍārr (the Bringer of Harm): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it and then asks God, exalted is He, for a need [that requires] the harming of a wrongdoer, sees in the sea of its operative deployment a means, and in the land of its operative deployment a wonder. His name, exalted is He, al-Nāfiʿ (the Bringer of Benefit): in it is a healing for every sick man and a restoration to health for every poor wretch. Whoever multiplies the remembrance of it in a state of harm, God, exalted is He, restores him to health from it. And if he be one possessed of a truthful [spiritual] state, and he persists in its remembrance until some of its worlds come into accord with him, he does not pass his hand over one who has been harmed but that God wipes away his harm. And so it is that whoever sets it in a square upon a signet-ring of silver, with the Moon in its exaltation — no one afflicted with an illness is sealed with it but that God, exalted is He, restores him to health from it. Do you not see that it points to His name, exalted is He, Muʿāfī (the Restorer to Health), and that the names of its letters point to two majestic names, namely Ilāh (God) [readingfor the edition's]and Shāfī (the Healer)? And this is its form, and it is as you see. Understand, and you will be rightly guided.
Fig. 25

His name, exalted is He, al-Nūr (the Light): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, illumines his heart. And when His name, exalted is He, al-Nāfiʿ is joined to it, it is a healing for every sickness and pain that arises from coldness. And when the Name is set in the square of the figure and water is poured over it, the one who suffers from coldness derives from it a far-reaching and manifest benefit; and it is preferable that the water be cast [upon it]. And God, glorified and exalted, knows best what is right. And this is the form of the square, as you see. [Wafq: cells as in the source — ] His name al-Hādī (the Guide) is a majestic name: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, the light of his heart increases and God guides [Fig. 26] his innermost secrets to knowledge of Him. And whoever is hard pressed by some affair among the affairs of this world, outward or inward, let him perform the ablution and pray two rakʿas with the Throne Verse and Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ, and let him make remembrance until his breath is cut off; then he is guided to what he seeks. His name, exalted is He, al-Badīʿ (the Wondrous Originator): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it does not cease to be an originator of the divine sciences and the secrets of religion. [His name al-Wārith (the Inheritor)]: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it and desires to inherit from one of his kinsmen or of his family, God, exalted is He, gives him to inherit what he seeks. His name, exalted is He, al-Bāqī (the Abiding): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, his final outcome is praised in all /fol. 50r./ his movements and his stillnesses. His name, exalted is He, al-Ṣabūr (the Patient): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, bestows upon him steadfastness in hardships, in weighty affairs, and in strange calamities, by the leave of God, glorified and exalted. And God, exalted is He, knows best.
